title: Don’t Sleep on This Specific $0-to-Millions Reselling Strategy
channel: Chris Koerner on The Koerner Office Podcast
promo_conflict: Guest runs a paid reseller mastermind ($5/month), which the host plugs. Both say no payment changed hands, and the guest says he earns nothing from the auction sites (B-Stock etc.). The guest also hands out deal links and posts on X, so he benefits from building an audience. The industrial and hinge deal numbers are partly hypothetical resale maths or second-hand student stories.

idea.name: Liquidation pallet/truckload reselling

idea.customer: Online marketplace buyers, plus bulk/wholesale buyers depending on category
idea.offer: Discounted brand-new or returned goods across categories (patio furniture, grills, fixtures, etc.)

ideas.delivery: Founder researches lots, bids with a spreadsheet 'product equation', takes delivery of pallets (warehouse or home), lists, ships, and handles returns.
ideas.other_uk_rules: UK has no resale permit, but VAT registration applies above threshold and HMRC platform reporting (DAC7) applies to marketplace sellers. Consumer Contracts Regs 2013 give 14-day distance-selling returns. Consumer Rights Act 2015 and GPSR/product safety apply to returned goods. US sources (Costco US, B-Stock US) mean import duty and freight.

uk_legal_risk.reason: Acquisition relies on scraping mobile numbers and mass-texting screen printers. Many UK print shops are sole traders or partnerships, and unsolicited marketing SMS to them is banned under PECR. Scraped mobile numbers are also personal data under UK GDPR.

ideas.other_uk_rules: Cold calls need TPS/CTPS screening; cold email only to limited companies with opt-out. The fake scarcity line ('this one's already gone') risks breaching the Business Protection from Misleading Marketing Regulations 2008. UK GDPR applies to scraped data.
